label: Kalki in the Puranas and Mahabharata
summary: Kalki is named as the tenth avatar of Vishnu in the Puranic lists, linked to the close of the Kali age. Accounts differ widely between and within the texts, and the game follows none of them.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Kalki in the Mahabharata (Markandeya passage)
summary: The Mahabharata mentions Kalki once, in a passage inside the Vana Parva that some scholars consider late. There he is a scholar-warrior who restores justice.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Kalki in the Garuda and Agni Puranas
summary: The Garuda Purana lists Kalki as the tenth avatar who ends the Kali age. The Agni Purana names his father as Vishnuyashas. The texts differ on his role.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: The Kalki Purana
summary: A late text, dated variously to between 1500 and the 18th century CE and thought to come from Bengal. It tells of Kalki born at Shambhala and a renewal of the cycle.
source: Wikipedia, 'Kalki' <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalki>, accessed 2026-11-22; text date is History, content is Tradition
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: A different end in the Vayu Purana
summary: The Vayu Purana gives the role of ending the Kali age to a figure named Pramiti, not Kalki. The Yuga Purana does not mention Kalki at all.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Kalki in Buddhist and Sikh texts
summary: The Buddhist Kalachakra Tantra (about the 9th-10th century CE) speaks of Kalki as a line of kings of Shambhala. Sikh scripture lists Kalki as an avatar in the Chaubis Avatar.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Kalki panels at Kanchipuram
summary: Temple reliefs at Kanchipuram show Kalki, which is early visual evidence that the idea was known in the south. The date of the reliefs needs checking.
source: Wikipedia, 'Kalki' <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalki>, accessed 2026-11-22 (reliefs mentioned; date not given on the page)

label: Length of the Kali Yuga in tradition
summary: Tradition counts the Kali age as 432,000 years. The game does not say our time is or is not that age, and makes no prediction.

label: The wheel turns again
summary: In the Puranic cycle, a new Satya age follows the Kali age, and the wheel of ages turns again. Texts describe renewal in different ways.
